_about: This file accompanies panel.json. Every leaf value here is a human-readable description of the metric at the same path in panel.json. See docs/tutorial/e2e_evaluation/metrics.md for the full design doc and recipes.
_legend: Wildcard placeholders: <column> = column name in the fused output, <attribute> = attribute name (same idea as <column>, used for fact-level metrics), <source> = source dataset name (e.g. products_1, products_2), <source_combo> = pipe-delimited combination of source names (e.g. 'products_1|products_2'), <pair> = source pair identifier (e.g. 'products_1__products_2'), <stage> = pipeline stage name (one of sm, norm, em_blocking, em_matching, refinement, fusion), <member> = ensemble member / strategy name. Reference levels: RF = Reference-Free (pipeline output evaluated on its own), SR = Silver Reference (pipeline output compared to a silver / baseline fused table), GR = Gold Reference (pipeline output compared to the human-curated gold fusion set). [0,1] means closed interval. 'higher is better' or 'lower is better' indicates the desired direction.
run_id: Caller-supplied identifier for this pipeline run (string). Used to disambiguate panels written for different configurations.
silver_source: Filesystem path to the silver-reference fused CSV that powers SR-level metrics (string). Null/absent if SR comparison was not performed.
gold_source: Filesystem path to the gold-reference fused CSV that powers GR-level metrics (string). Null/absent if GR comparison was not performed.

RF.composite_score: Single-number summary of pipeline quality at the Reference-Free level, combining coverage, consistency, and structural signals that do not require a reference table. Float in [0, 1], higher is better. See composite_score.json for the recipe and weights.

SR.bcubed_f1: Shorthand for correctness.cluster.SR.bcubed.f1: BCubed F1 of pipeline clusters against silver-reference clusters. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
SR.macro_accuracy: Shorthand for correctness.fact.SR.macro_accuracy: unweighted mean of per-attribute accuracy against silver. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
SR.composite_score: Single-number summary of pipeline quality at the Silver-Reference level. Float in [0, 1], higher is better. See composite_score.json for the recipe and weights.

GR.bcubed_f1: Shorthand for correctness.cluster.GR.bcubed.f1: BCubed F1 of pipeline clusters against gold-reference clusters. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
GR.macro_accuracy: Shorthand for correctness.fact.GR.macro_accuracy: unweighted mean of per-attribute accuracy against gold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
GR.composite_score: Single-number summary of pipeline quality at the Gold-Reference level. Float in [0, 1], higher is better. See composite_score.json for the recipe and weights.

RF.n_rows_output: Number of rows in the fused pipeline output. Non-negative integer.
RF.n_rows_largest_input: Row count of the largest input source feeding fusion. Non-negative integer. Reference point for assessing whether fusion produced consolidation or inflation.
RF.row_gain_vs_largest_input: (n_rows_output - n_rows_largest_input) / n_rows_largest_input. Float; positive means the fused table has more rows than the largest input (possible over-splitting or unmatched additions), negative means consolidation.

SR.n_reference: Number of rows in the silver-reference fused table. Non-negative integer.
SR.row_count_abs_diff: Absolute difference between pipeline row count and reference row count: |n_pipe - n_reference|. Non-negative integer.
SR.row_count_rel_diff: Relative row-count difference: row_count_abs_diff / n_reference. Non-negative float; lower is closer to reference cardinality.
SR.n_recovered: Number of reference clusters fully recovered by the pipeline (every member of the reference cluster ends up in a single pipeline cluster that contains no other reference members). Non-negative integer, higher is better.
SR.n_partial: Number of reference clusters partially recovered (some but not all members mapped to a single pipeline cluster, or mapped across multiple pipeline clusters). Non-negative integer.
SR.n_lost: Number of reference clusters with no overlap into any pipeline cluster. Non-negative integer, lower is better.
SR.n_fabricated: Number of pipeline clusters that do not align with any reference cluster (introduced by the pipeline beyond what the reference represents). Non-negative integer.
SR.recovery_rate: n_recovered / n_reference. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.

GR.n_reference: Number of rows in the gold-reference fused table. Non-negative integer.
GR.row_count_abs_diff: Absolute difference between pipeline row count and gold row count. Non-negative integer.
GR.row_count_rel_diff: row_count_abs_diff / n_reference at the GR level. Non-negative float; lower is closer to gold cardinality. Often large because gold tables typically cover only a fraction of the input universe.
GR.n_recovered: Number of gold clusters fully recovered by the pipeline. Non-negative integer, higher is better.
GR.n_partial: Number of gold clusters partially recovered. Non-negative integer.
GR.n_lost: Number of gold clusters with no overlap into any pipeline cluster. Non-negative integer, lower is better.
GR.n_fabricated: Number of pipeline clusters that do not align with any gold cluster. Non-negative integer; commonly large because gold covers only a small slice of the population.
GR.recovery_rate: n_recovered / n_reference at the GR level. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.

RF.density_output: Fraction of non-null cells in the fused output across all evaluated attributes: non_null_cells / (n_rows * n_attrs). Float in [0, 1], higher means denser table.
RF.density_largest_input: Same density measure computed on the largest input source. Float in [0, 1].
RF.density_gain: density_output - density_largest_input. Float in [-1, 1]; positive means fusion filled in more cells than the largest input had on its own.

per_column_drift_normalized.<column>: Normalized drift of the pipeline's distribution for this column vs the silver-reference distribution (e.g., Jensen-Shannon for categoricals, normalized 1D Wasserstein-like distance for numerics). Float in [0, 1], lower is better (0 = identical distributions).

SR.overall_drift: Mean of per-column normalized drift values across all evaluated columns. Float in [0, 1], lower is better.

<column>.reference_density: Fraction of non-null cells for this column in the silver reference. Float in [0, 1].
<column>.pipe_density: Fraction of non-null cells for this column in the pipeline output. Float in [0, 1].
<column>.delta: pipe_density - reference_density. Float in [-1, 1]; positive means the pipeline fills this column more often than silver does.

per_column_drift_normalized.<column>: Normalized distributional drift of the pipeline vs the gold reference for this column. Float in [0, 1], lower is better.

GR.overall_drift: Mean of per-column normalized drift values vs gold. Float in [0, 1], lower is better.

<column>.reference_density: Fraction of non-null cells for this column in the gold reference. Float in [0, 1].
<column>.pipe_density: Fraction of non-null cells for this column in the pipeline output. Float in [0, 1].

source_based.RF: Source-based coverage requires cell-level provenance; empty dict when no provenance is available at the Reference-Free level (currently always empty by design).

same_source_collision_rate.reference: Fraction of silver-reference clusters that contain two or more rows from the same source. Float in [0, 1]; high values indicate the reference itself permits same-source duplicates within an entity cluster.
same_source_collision_rate.pipe: Same metric computed on pipeline clusters. Float in [0, 1].
same_source_collision_rate.delta: pipe - reference. Float in [-1, 1]; positive means the pipeline produces more same-source collisions than silver.

<source>.reference: Same-source collision rate restricted to this source in the silver reference. Float in [0, 1].
<source>.pipe: Same-source collision rate restricted to this source in the pipeline output. Float in [0, 1].
<source>.delta: pipe - reference for this source. Float in [-1, 1].

SR.source_mix_distribution_js: Jensen-Shannon divergence between the pipeline's distribution over source-mix combinations and silver's distribution. Float in [0, 1], lower is better.

<source>.reference: Fraction of silver clusters that contain at least one row from this source. Float in [0, 1].
<source>.pipe: Fraction of pipeline clusters that contain at least one row from this source. Float in [0, 1].

source_mix_distribution_reference.<source_combo>: Proportion of silver clusters whose constituent rows come from this exact pipe-delimited source combination. Float in [0, 1]; proportions across all keys sum to 1.

source_mix_distribution_pipe.<source_combo>: Proportion of pipeline clusters whose constituent rows come from this exact pipe-delimited source combination. Float in [0, 1]; proportions across all keys sum to 1.

same_source_collision_rate.reference: Fraction of gold clusters that contain two or more rows from the same source. Float in [0, 1].
same_source_collision_rate.pipe: Same metric on pipeline clusters. Float in [0, 1].

<source>.reference: Same-source collision rate restricted to this source in the gold reference. Float in [0, 1].
<source>.pipe: Same-source collision rate restricted to this source in the pipeline output. Float in [0, 1].
<source>.delta: pipe - reference for this source. Float in [-1, 1].

GR.source_mix_distribution_js: Jensen-Shannon divergence between the pipeline's source-mix distribution and gold's. Float in [0, 1], lower is better.

<source>.reference: Fraction of gold clusters that contain at least one row from this source. Float in [0, 1].
<source>.pipe: Fraction of pipeline clusters that contain at least one row from this source. Float in [0, 1].

source_mix_distribution_reference.<source_combo>: Proportion of gold clusters whose constituent rows come from this exact pipe-delimited source combination. Float in [0, 1].

source_mix_distribution_pipe.<source_combo>: Proportion of pipeline clusters whose constituent rows come from this exact pipe-delimited source combination. Float in [0, 1].

<column>.validity_rate_pipe: Fraction of non-null cells in this column of the pipeline output that pass type-parse and declared constraints. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<column>.parse_failures_pipe: Count of non-null cells in the pipeline output that failed type parsing for this column. Non-negative integer, lower is better.
<column>.constraint_failures_pipe: Count of non-null cells that parsed but violated a declared constraint (e.g., range, enum). Non-negative integer, lower is better.
<column>.n_evaluated_pipe: Number of non-null cells evaluated for validity in this column. Non-negative integer.

consistency._design_extensions_pending: Free-text design note explaining that broader consistency checks (ontology-style disjointness, cross-attribute constraints) are still pending; validity_per_column is currently the only first-class consistency signal. String.

<column>.validity_rate_pipe: Fraction of non-null pipeline cells in this column that pass validity checks. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<column>.validity_rate_reference: Same fraction computed on the silver reference. Float in [0, 1].
<column>.delta: validity_rate_pipe - validity_rate_reference. Float in [-1, 1]; positive means the pipeline is more valid than silver on this column.
<column>.parse_failures_pipe: Count of parse failures in the pipeline output for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.parse_failures_reference: Count of parse failures in the silver reference for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.constraint_failures_pipe: Count of constraint violations in the pipeline output for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.constraint_failures_reference: Count of constraint violations in the silver reference for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.n_evaluated_pipe: Number of non-null pipeline cells evaluated. Non-negative integer.
<column>.n_evaluated_reference: Number of non-null silver cells evaluated. Non-negative integer.

SR.mean_validity_delta: Unweighted mean over columns of (validity_rate_pipe - validity_rate_reference). Float in [-1, 1]; positive means the pipeline is on average more valid than silver.

<column>.validity_rate_pipe: Fraction of non-null pipeline cells in this column that pass validity checks. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<column>.validity_rate_reference: Same fraction computed on the gold reference. Float in [0, 1].
<column>.parse_failures_pipe: Count of parse failures in the pipeline output for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.parse_failures_reference: Count of parse failures in the gold reference for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.constraint_failures_pipe: Count of constraint violations in the pipeline output for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.constraint_failures_reference: Count of constraint violations in the gold reference for this column. Non-negative integer.
<column>.n_evaluated_pipe: Number of non-null pipeline cells evaluated. Non-negative integer.
<column>.n_evaluated_reference: Number of non-null gold cells evaluated. Non-negative integer.

GR.mean_validity_delta: Unweighted mean over columns of (validity_rate_pipe - validity_rate_reference) vs gold. Float in [-1, 1].

bcubed.precision: BCubed precision of pipeline clusters against silver clusters: for each pipeline-clustered row, the fraction of its cluster-mates that share its silver cluster, averaged over rows. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
bcubed.recall: BCubed recall against silver: for each row, the fraction of its silver cluster-mates that also share its pipeline cluster, averaged over rows. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
bcubed.f1: Harmonic mean of bcubed.precision and bcubed.recall against silver. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.

alignment.mean_jaccard: Mean Jaccard similarity between each silver cluster and its best-matching pipeline cluster (matched 1:1). Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
alignment.matched_cluster_rate_at_threshold: Fraction of silver clusters whose best-matching pipeline cluster exceeds the Jaccard threshold given by matched_threshold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
alignment.matched_threshold: Jaccard threshold used by matched_cluster_rate_at_threshold (typically 0.5). Float in [0, 1].
alignment.size_match_rate: Fraction of silver clusters whose best-matching pipeline cluster has the same size. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
alignment.mean_size_delta: Mean of (pipeline_cluster_size - silver_cluster_size) across matched silver clusters. Float; negative means pipeline clusters are on average smaller than silver, positive means larger.
alignment.max_size_overshoot: Maximum value of (pipeline_cluster_size - silver_cluster_size) across matched clusters. Integer; positive values indicate at least one pipeline cluster substantially larger than its silver counterpart, negative values indicate the worst undershoot.

bcubed.precision: BCubed precision of pipeline clusters against gold clusters. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
bcubed.recall: BCubed recall of pipeline clusters against gold clusters. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
bcubed.f1: Harmonic mean of bcubed.precision and bcubed.recall against gold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.

alignment.mean_jaccard: Mean Jaccard similarity between each gold cluster and its best-matching pipeline cluster. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
alignment.matched_cluster_rate_at_threshold: Fraction of gold clusters whose best-matching pipeline cluster exceeds the matched_threshold Jaccard. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
alignment.matched_threshold: Jaccard threshold used by matched_cluster_rate_at_threshold for the GR level. Float in [0, 1].
alignment.size_match_rate: Fraction of gold clusters whose best-matching pipeline cluster has the same size. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
alignment.mean_size_delta: Mean of (pipeline_cluster_size - gold_cluster_size) across matched gold clusters. Float.
alignment.max_size_overshoot: Maximum value of (pipeline_cluster_size - gold_cluster_size) across matched gold clusters. Integer.

<attribute>.accuracy: Fraction of paired (pipeline, silver) cells for this attribute that match exactly (after normalization). Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.count: Number of paired cells used to compute accuracy for this attribute. Non-negative integer.
<attribute>.similarity_mean: Mean string/value similarity between paired pipeline and silver cells for this attribute. Float in [0, 1], higher is better. Useful for text fields where exact match is too strict.
<attribute>.mae: Mean absolute error between paired numeric cells (numeric attributes only). Non-negative float, lower is better. Units are the attribute's native units.
<attribute>.medae: Median absolute error between paired numeric cells (numeric attributes only). Non-negative float, lower is better.
<attribute>.pct_within_tolerance: Fraction of paired cells whose value is within the declared tolerance band (numeric attributes, or categoricals with a tolerance). Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.accuracy_similarity_gap: similarity_mean - accuracy (text attributes only, emitted when this gap is notably large). Float; large positive values suggest the pipeline values are semantically close but not exact, often due to normalization differences.
<attribute>.mismatch_fingerprint: Short categorical tag describing the dominant kind of mismatch (text attributes only, emitted when accuracy_similarity_gap is large). String, e.g. 'normalization_difference_suspected'.

SR.macro_accuracy: Unweighted mean across attributes of per_attribute.accuracy. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
SR.micro_accuracy: Cell-weighted mean of per-attribute accuracy: sum of matching cells over sum of paired cells across attributes. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
SR.conflict_only_accuracy: Macro-accuracy restricted to attributes where the source rows disagreed (i.e., fusion actually had to choose among conflicting values). Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
SR.conflict_only_micro_accuracy: Cell-weighted accuracy restricted to conflict cells. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.

<attribute>.accuracy: Accuracy on conflict-only cells for this attribute. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.count: Number of conflict-only paired cells for this attribute. Non-negative integer.

SR.conflict_rate_pipe: Fraction of paired cells across all attributes where the underlying source rows disagreed, computed on the pipeline-side cluster groupings. Float in [0, 1].
SR.conflict_rate_reference: Same conflict rate computed on the silver-side cluster groupings. Float in [0, 1].
SR.fully_correct_cluster_rate: Fraction of pipeline clusters whose fused row matches the corresponding silver row on every evaluated attribute. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
SR.list_attribute_set_metrics: Dict of set-based metrics (precision/recall/F1 over set-valued attributes); empty when no list/set attributes are evaluated.

<attribute>.accuracy: Fraction of paired (pipeline, gold) cells for this attribute that match exactly. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.count: Number of paired cells used to compute accuracy for this attribute. Non-negative integer.
<attribute>.similarity_mean: Mean string/value similarity between paired pipeline and gold cells for this attribute. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.mae: Mean absolute error between paired numeric cells (numeric attributes only). Non-negative float, lower is better.
<attribute>.medae: Median absolute error between paired numeric cells (numeric attributes only). Non-negative float, lower is better.
<attribute>.pct_within_tolerance: Fraction of paired cells whose value is within the declared tolerance band. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.accuracy_similarity_gap: similarity_mean - accuracy (text attributes, when the gap is large). Float; flags normalization-style mismatches against gold.
<attribute>.mismatch_fingerprint: Short categorical tag describing the dominant kind of text mismatch. String.

GR.macro_accuracy: Unweighted mean across attributes of per_attribute.accuracy against gold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
GR.micro_accuracy: Cell-weighted mean of per-attribute accuracy against gold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
GR.conflict_only_accuracy: Macro-accuracy restricted to attributes where the source rows disagreed at the gold-aligned clusters. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
GR.conflict_only_micro_accuracy: Cell-weighted accuracy on conflict-only cells, evaluated against gold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.

<attribute>.accuracy: Accuracy on conflict-only cells for this attribute, evaluated against gold. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
<attribute>.count: Number of conflict-only paired cells for this attribute. Non-negative integer.

GR.conflict_rate_pipe: Fraction of paired cells with disagreeing source values on the pipeline side. Float in [0, 1].
GR.conflict_rate_reference: Same conflict rate on the gold side. Float in [0, 1].
GR.fully_correct_cluster_rate: Fraction of pipeline clusters whose fused row matches the corresponding gold row on every evaluated attribute. Float in [0, 1], higher is better.
GR.list_attribute_set_metrics: Dict of set-based metrics for list/set-valued attributes; empty when none are evaluated.

<stage>.stage: Canonical name of this pipeline stage. String, one of: sm | norm | em_blocking | em_matching | refinement | fusion.
<stage>.winner: Name of the strategy / member selected for this stage by the orchestrator. String.
<stage>.metric_key: Name of the metric used to choose the winner at this stage (e.g., 'f1', 'recall', 'macro_accuracy'). String.
<stage>.val_score: Score of the winning strategy on the validation surface for this stage, using metric_key. Float; range/direction depend on metric_key.
<stage>.test_score: Score of the winning strategy on the held-out test surface for this stage, using metric_key. Float; range/direction depend on metric_key.

per_member_val.<member>: Validation-surface score for this committee member / candidate strategy at this stage. Float; range/direction depend on metric_key.

per_member_test.<member>: Test-surface score for this committee member / candidate strategy at this stage. Float; range/direction depend on metric_key.

<stage>.runtime_s: Wall-clock seconds spent on this stage. Non-negative float, seconds.

notes.test_eq_val: True iff the SM stage reused the validation surface as its test surface (no held-out SM test split). Boolean.
notes.test_eq_val_reason: Free-text explanation for why test_eq_val is true (e.g., 'no held-out SM test split for baseline'). String.

notes.applied_to_downstream: True iff the chosen normalization was actually propagated to downstream stages (EM, fusion). Boolean.
notes.spread: Spread (max - min) of normalization-candidate scores across members on the validation surface. Float; near-zero spread indicates the choice was vacuous.
notes.vacuous: True iff the normalization choice is considered vacuous (spread < vacuous_epsilon). Boolean.
notes.vacuous_epsilon: Epsilon used to flag a vacuous normalization choice. Float, non-negative.

em_blocking._metric_key_note: For em_blocking, metric_key / val_score / test_score now report pair_completeness (recall — fraction of true gold pairs the blocker preserves). reduction_ratio remains the per-pair tiebreaker inside the composition selection strategy and is surfaced as a secondary side metric under notes.per_member_reduction_ratio_{val,test}.

per_pair_winner.<pair>: Winning blocker for this source pair. String (blocker name).

notes.selection_strategy: Description of how the blocker was chosen per source pair (e.g., 'composition (per-pair: pair_completeness >= 0.97, reduction_ratio tiebreak)'). String.
notes.val_split_available: True iff a validation split was available for blocker selection. Boolean.
notes.test_split_available: True iff a held-out test split was available for blocker evaluation. Boolean.
notes.recall_floor: Minimum pair_completeness (recall) a blocker must clear to be eligible at this stage; below the floor the candidate is rejected. Float in [0, 1].

per_member_reduction_ratio_val.<member>: Validation-surface reduction_ratio for this blocker, exposed as a secondary side metric (fraction of all possible pairs the blocker prunes). Float in [0, 1].

per_member_reduction_ratio_test.<member>: Test-surface reduction_ratio for this blocker (mirrors val when there is no separate test pass; see notes.test_split_available). Float in [0, 1].

notes.val_split_available: True iff a validation split was available for matcher selection. Boolean.
notes.test_split_available: True iff a held-out test split was available for matcher evaluation. Boolean.
notes.clustering_applied_within_em: Name of the clustering / link-resolution strategy applied inside the EM stage (e.g., 'greedy', 'mbm', 'none'). String.

notes.methods_competed: Names of the refinement methods that competed at this stage. List of strings (e.g., ['baseline', 'greedy', 'mbm']).
notes.n_correspondences: Number of pairwise correspondences considered by the refinement step. Non-negative integer.

notes.val_surface_available: True iff a validation fusion surface was available to score fusion strategies. Boolean.
notes.n_fused_rows: Number of rows produced by the fusion stage. Non-negative integer.
notes.n_correspondences_used: Number of pairwise correspondences fed into fusion (after refinement). Non-negative integer.

aggregated._placeholder: Flag indicating that the aggregated section is a placeholder pending the two-dimensional (Quality x Reference) weighting design. Boolean.
aggregated._design_intent: Free-text note describing the planned design: a 2D weighted aggregate (Quality x Reference). Until then, headline.<level>.composite_score carries a per-reference-level single-axis composite. String.

warnings: List of free-form diagnostic strings emitted during panel construction. Each entry flags a situation that may affect interpretation, for example: a metric block was skipped because a required input (such as cell_provenance) was not supplied; a reference comparison was disabled because the reference file was missing; a stage's test surface fell back to its validation surface; a column failed to parse for validity checks; or a committee had only one viable member. Treat each entry as a hint to inspect that specific area before trusting downstream numbers.

resource_usage.duration_seconds: Total wall-clock duration of the pipeline run that produced this panel. Non-negative float, seconds.

api_tokens.input_tokens: Total input tokens consumed across all counted LLM calls in this run. Non-negative integer.
api_tokens.output_tokens: Total output tokens generated across all counted LLM calls in this run. Non-negative integer.
api_tokens.total_tokens: input_tokens + output_tokens across all counted LLM calls. Non-negative integer.
api_tokens.n_calls: Total number of counted LLM API calls in this run. Non-negative integer.

resource_usage.api_notes: Free-text summary of which stages contributed to the api_tokens totals and which were skipped (e.g., non-LLM winners), with the per-stage token/call counts noted in parentheses. String.
